newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends mostly lower as supplies increase.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends mostly lower as supplies increase.

text.p: Confirmation Wednesday by USDA that world wheat stocks were increasing again pressured CBOT wheat futures to a lower close, traders said.
The government's U.S. and world supply/demand reports Wednesday continued to weigh on the wheat market, they said.

USDA this week said world wheat ending stocks for the 1996-97 marketing year would total 117.43 million tonnes, up from 108.68 million tonnes forecast by the government in August. Export concerns also hit prices with competition from Canada, Australia, Argentina and the EU a driving force in the wheat futures market.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 17,000 contracts, down from 18,364 Wednesday, according to the CBOT.
In wheat options, The Chicago Corp bought 200 December $4.60 puts at 31 cents, ADM Investor Services bought 100 December $4.80 calls at 4 to 4-1/4 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 4,500 contracts, up slightly from 4,058 Wednesday.
Wheat futures closed six cents per bushel lower to 2-3/4 higher, with September down six at $4.38.
